stories.headline: Team Carlzyn scored 45.40
stories.body:
Team Carlzyn has 45.40 on the board in week five with Josh Allen still to play on Monday night, trailing Return of the King 143.62. The matchup needs 98.2 points from one quarterback.

Three of the men Mason started carry an Out designation on Sleeper: David Montgomery with a groin, Deebo Samuel with a hamstring and TreVeyon Henderson with an ankle. Between them they returned 8.40. This desk does not mock an injury and will not pretend to know what happened in any of those three games.

The rest of the lineup was healthy. Jonathan Taylor returned 11.20 against a projection of 19.2, DK Metcalf 5.30, Jake Ferguson 4.90, Carnell Tate 1.60. Woody Marks (12.50) and Hunter Henry (13.40) each outscored every man who started ahead of them. Keenan Allen (9.50) outscored nine of the ten.

Week four was the quieter version of the same week. Carlzyn scored 96.52, lost to Kool-Aid Man by 9.50, and left 85.4 unstarted with 28.0 of it on Kyle Monangai. The season reads 168.0, 142.1, 95.6, 96.5, and now this. They are 2-2, tenth in the power rankings, and carry a 33% playoff estimate. Stephen B Smith picked them to win the championship and said in week three that he could not move off it.

takes.text: FORTY-FIVE POINT FOUR OH! No, I am not moving off it, and I will tell you exactly why, because three of those men were listed OUT and his quarterback has not played yet! You want to score a lineup that was never on the field? Score it! But do not come to me with forty-five and tell me the roster is the problem, because the roster is sitting in a training room!

There it is. The defence of the pick is that the team was too injured to be measured. I said in September that fourth is where you hide a team you are afraid to defend. The man who took it from there is now defending a forty-five.

Separate the two things, because they are separate. Three starters listed Out is not variance, it is a lineup submitted with three known holes in it, and the 80% start/sit for the season is the lowest figure in this league outside of Darrien. What is variance is the healthy half: Taylor at 11.20 off a 19.2, Metcalf at 5.30, Ferguson at 4.90. Those four decisions cost him nothing in process and everything on the scoreboard, and that is the part I would not punish him for.

I have been in the room on the week where a man stops opening the app. You can tell from the lineup, not from the score. The score was always going to be ugly with three men out. What tells you where he is at is Hunter Henry sitting on a bench at thirteen four while a tight end he had no reason to trust started ahead of him. That is a man who filled the card out on Thursday and did not go back to it.

Forty-five point four oh is not a bad week. A bad week is a hundred and ten. Forty-five is a SIGN. This is what happens to a roster that was built to win in December and I would like the room to remember that Josh Allen has not played, so the real number is closer to seventy, and seventy is a Tuesday. I am not worried about Mason. I am worried about the man who picked him on television.

stories.storyline: Does Smith's pick survive a healthy week, or is 45.40 the number the rest of the season gets measured against?

stories.headline: Ian is 4-0 and not one man on this desk picked him
stories.body:
littlescot229 beat Chop Wood, Carry Water 163.38 to 159.50 in week four and is the only undefeated team left in this league. Ian is first in the standings, carries a 100% playoff estimate, and his 50% chance at the top seed is the highest on the board.

He got there by leaving 10.6 points unstarted, the lowest figure in the league in week four, against Blake's 71.5 — which included 23.6 from Keon Coleman in a game Blake lost by 3.88. Ian's all-play record is 34-10, identical to Blake's.

Five analysts named a champion in week two. Shannon Larp took F&F: Tokyo Swift, Stephen B Smith took Team Carlzyn, Mina Crimes took I HURT MY NABERS, Skip Baseless took Chop Wood, Carry Water and Fat McCafferty took The Shortbus Superstars. Nobody took the 4-0 team.

In week five he leads Dsteady1234 145.14 to 108.74 with only his defense left to play. Jared Goff returned 34.94 and Jahmyr Gibbs 37.70, which is 72.64 from two Detroit players on a roster the desk spent September describing as a two-player Thursday.

takes.text: Nobody picked him because there is nothing to pick. There is no ceiling argument here, no roster anybody wants to talk about, no draft nobody can get over. There is a man who sets his lineup, takes the points, and has left ten and a half on the bench in a week where the second-best team in this league left seventy-one. Four and nought is not an accident when it looks like that.

Four and nought and second in the rankings, which tells you what the rankings think of it. Blake has fifty-one more points than him and the same all-play record, and he lost that game by three point eight eight with twenty-three points of Keon Coleman on his bench. I am not moving off Chop Wood, Carry Water because the only thing between those two teams is the week Blake forgot to look at his flex.

I will tell you why nobody picked him and nobody in this building has the nerve to say it. The team is called littlescot229. That is not a team name, that is a password. You cannot put that on a championship trophy and everybody on this desk knew it in September, so we all went and found a team with a NAME. He is four and nought and he is going to win this league with a username and it is going to be the funniest thing that has ever happened here.

stories.storyline: Does anybody on the desk credit the 4-0 team before it stops being 4-0?

stories.headline: The desk told the commissioner to bench Drake Maye. He did it once and lost by 14.26.
stories.body:
In week four, Drake Maye scored 33.2 on Egbukkake's bench. Adam lost to The Shortbus Superstars 165.84 to 151.58, a margin of 14.26, with 93.7 points unstarted.

In week five Maye is back in the lineup and has returned 47.46 against a projection of 22.1. It is the highest individual score on any roster in this league this week, and Egbukkake leads I HURT MY NABERS 152.56 to 117.76 with the matchup decided.

This desk spent two editions pointing at the quarterbacks Adam bought for three dollars and never played. The week he finally moved off Maye is the week Maye was the best player on his bench. He is 1-3 with 538.18 points for, fifth-most in the league, a luck rating of -0.9, tenth in the standings and fourth in the power rankings, and a 54% playoff estimate higher than four of the six 2-2 teams sitting above him in the table.

takes.text: FORTY-SEVEN POINT FOUR SIX! And where was this man in week four! On the BENCH! Thirty-three points on the bench in a game he lost by fourteen! I want to be very clear about what happened here, because the commissioner did exactly what this desk told him to do, it cost him a football game, and then he ignored us and got the highest score in the league. That is not vindication. That is an accident with a smile on it.

I said a few weeks ago that going back to the same quarterback every week had stopped being loyalty and started being a habit he had not examined. I was wrong about which part was the habit. He examined it, he sat the man, and the man went for thirty-three. The lesson is not that we were wrong about the process, it is that a process you change in one week to make a desk stop shouting at you is not a process.

Nought and three to one and three with a hundred and fifty-two, fifth in the league in points scored, fourth in the rankings, and he has been sat in the basement of the standings the whole time because of a luck number. I have been telling this desk since week two that the commissioner is alive. Fifty-four percent. Write it down.

stories.storyline: Does Maye stay in the lineup now, and does fourth in the rankings ever turn into fourth in the standings?

stories.headline: Boesch finally started Tyler Shough and left 29.28 of Jordan Love on the bench
stories.body:
Week four was the best week of Boesch's season. The Shortbus Superstars scored 165.84, beat Egbukkake, and took their scoring line to 100.6, 104.1, 140.1, 165.8 — up every single week. They are 2-2 with a 54% playoff estimate, eighth in the power rankings, and a last-three scoring figure of 136.7 that beats the third-ranked team's.

Week five went the other way. He started Tyler Shough, the quarterback he traded TreVeyon Henderson for in week three, and Shough returned 1.84. Jordan Love scored 29.28 on the bench, a gap of 27.44. MarShawn Lloyd, the $5 claim he won this week, scored 16.70 on the bench. Terry McLaurin 12.20, Xavier Hutchinson 10.50. That is 68.68 unstarted in a game he trails 128.20 to 98.54.

He benched Shough for 32.80 in week three and won. He started him for 1.84 in week five and needs 29.7 from Puka Nacua on Monday night to save it. Henderson, the other half of that trade, started for Team Carlzyn carrying an Out designation.

takes.text: A hundred, a hundred and four, a hundred and forty, a hundred and sixty-five. Four weeks, four improvements, two and two, fifty-four percent, and the room is going to spend this morning talking about one quarterback. I picked this team when the room laughed. The room is not laughing, the room is changing the subject, and those are different things.

In week three I said he traded for a quarterback and would not start him. He has now started him, and the quarterback scored one point eight four, and the running back he gave up for him was listed Out and started anyway for somebody else. Both halves of that trade played this weekend and the two of them produced under seven points between them. That is not a trade, that is a mutual surrender.

Sixty-eight points unstarted and a twenty-seven point gap at the single position he had a decision to make at. The frustrating part is that it is the fourth week in a row this roster has had more points available than it started, and the trend line is still up, which means the scoring is coming from the roster improving rather than from the lineup getting better. One of those two things he controls.

stories.storyline: Does Nacua save it on Monday, and does Shough start again if he does not?

stories.headline: Darrien fixed the bench and lost by 43.18
stories.body:
A week after leaving 102.0 points unstarted, Dsteady1234 left 39.1. He scored 117.48, his second-best week of the season, and lost to F&F: Tokyo Swift 160.66 to 117.48.

He is 0-4. He has the fewest points in the league at 437.12, the most points against at 568.42, an all-play record of 6-38, and the hardest schedule faced of anybody at 140.1 — which is the one line on his page that is nobody's fault. His playoff estimate is 0% with ten weeks left, the only zero on the board.

He has also not spent a dollar of his $100, one of five teams in this league that has moved no money at all. In week four he dropped De'Von Achane and added Isaiah Davis. In week five Davis started for 2.70 and Efton Chism, added the same week, scored 10.90 from the bench alongside 15.20 from Kyle Pitts.

takes.text: I said this was fixable in forty minutes on a Sunday morning. He spent the forty minutes. The bench went from a hundred and two to thirty-nine, the score went up thirty points, and he lost by forty-three. That is the cruellest thing this league has done to anybody this season, and the only thing I can tell him is that the forty minutes were still the right forty minutes.

Six and thirty-eight on all-play with the hardest schedule faced in the league. Those two facts fight each other and the all-play one wins: a team that has beaten six of forty-four opportunities is not a schedule victim, it is the twelfth team. The zero percent is not a punishment for week four, it is four weeks of scoring that nothing in the remaining ten can outrun. He is also the only man here who has not made a claim, and at nought and four there is nothing left to protect the hundred dollars for.

stories.storyline: Does Darrien ever spend the $100, or does 0% become the whole season?

stories.headline: Ian bought three tight ends for $60 and is starting neither of them
stories.body:
littlescot229 won three tight ends on week four waivers: Mike Gesicki for $25, Pat Freiermuth for $20 and Tyler Higbee for $15. That is $60, the whole of his season's spending and the most money anybody in this league has moved.

In week five he started Tyler Warren and Harold Fannin. Warren returned 21.40 and Fannin 1.40. Freiermuth scored 21.50 from the bench, more than either of them. Gesicki scored 7.40 from the bench. Higbee is a Ram and has not played yet.

He also bid $15 on Aaron Rodgers in the same run of claims and lost him to a $10 bid from davidbatista. Rodgers returned 28.00 for David in week five. Ian is 4-0 with $40 left.

takes.text: Sixty dollars across three men at one position in one week, and the position he actually had covered. The outcome so far is that the most expensive of the three is on the bench at seven four and the second most expensive outscored both starters by a tenth of a point. I would not call it a bad process — he identified a thin position and bought depth into it — but the $15 he lost on Rodgers is the bid that would have mattered, and he lost it by five dollars to a man who is 2-2.

SIXTY DOLLARS OF TIGHT ENDS! He has five of them! FIVE! He is starting two of them and the one he paid twenty for is on the BENCH outscoring the two he picked! And he is four and nought, which is the part that makes me want to throw something, because nothing this man does makes sense and the standings do not care!

The best record in this league belongs to the man with the worst shopping in it, and I want everybody to hold both of those at once. He spent sixty dollars solving a problem he did not have and lost the fifteen-dollar bid that would have got him a quarterback who went for twenty-eight. He is four and nought in spite of the chequebook, not because of it.

stories.storyline: Does any of Ian's $60 of tight ends ever make his starting lineup?

stories.headline: The McCaffrey trade's first weekend went to the man who is 1-3
stories.body:
Return of the King and I HURT MY NABERS traded in week five. Tyler got Christian McCaffrey and Tucker Kraft. Chase got A.J. Brown and Trey McBride.

Tyler started both of his. McCaffrey returned 17.30 and Kraft 11.60, and Return of the King has 143.62 on the board — his best week since the opener, after 148.0, 122.7, 122.7 and 117.5 — against Team Carlzyn's 45.40.

Chase started McBride, who returned 21.60, and left A.J. Brown on the bench in a game he is losing by 34.80. I HURT MY NABERS is Mina Crimes's championship pick, sixth in the power rankings with a 37% playoff estimate, and has now scored under 140 in four straight weeks after opening the season with 177.8.

takes.text: Two men made the same trade for opposite reasons. One of them is one and three and needed the two best players he could get his hands on this week. The other is two and two and was buying for a position he thinks he wins in November. Both of those are defensible and only one of them had to be right on Sunday, which is why the one and three man looks like the winner this morning and might not in six weeks.

He traded for A.J. Brown and did not start him. I have now typed that sentence about three different managers in this league in three weeks and I am starting to think the trade button and the lineup page are hosted on separate websites.

Christian McCaffrey to a one and three team in week five. Everybody wants to call that desperate and I am calling it the first man in this league to notice there are ten weeks left. He put up a hundred and forty-three. That is not a man selling his season, that is a man who looked at twenty-five percent and decided twenty-five percent was worth playing for. Write it down.

stories.storyline: Does Tyler's 25% become a playoff run, or does Chase win the trade in November?

stories.headline: The commissioner paid $21 for a running back listed Out and started him anyway
stories.body:
Egbukkake won Will Shipley on week four waivers for $21, outbidding F&F: Tokyo Swift at $12. It is more than Adam had spent all season to that point.

Shipley is in the week five lineup carrying an Out designation on his foot and has returned 8.30. Adam also started the Dallas Cowboys, a $0 claim from the same run, for 1.00.

Meanwhile C.J. Stroud, whom Adam bought for $1 in week three, was claimed by Chop Wood, Carry Water for nothing in week five and has returned 22.94 — with Patrick Mahomes sitting on Blake's bench. Kyler Murray, the $2 claim from the same week, was dropped in week four. Adam has spent $30, has $70 left, and is winning this week by 34.80 anyway.

takes.text: He paid a DOLLAR for C.J. Stroud and let him go, and Blake picked him up for NOTHING and the man has twenty-two ninety-four! The commissioner bought a quarterback, declined to play him, and handed him to the team at the top of the rankings for free! At some point somebody in that league office has to ask who is doing the shopping!

Twenty-one dollars is a defensible number for a back in that situation and the $12 underbid says the market agreed. Starting him with an Out designation beside his name is the part I would flag, and in fairness it returned 8.30 against a 10.5 projection, so it cost him almost nothing. The actual loss on the ledger is a dollar: he bought the quarterback who is currently starting for the best team in this league and let him walk for free.

stories.storyline: Does Adam's $30 of shopping show up anywhere other than another team's lineup?
